answer.note: Estimated energy released at the atomic bomb explosion, $E \approx 3 \cdot 10^{12}\ J$, from the fit $A = 0.42$, $B = 2.48$.

solution.statement:
**Marking scheme**

Any other solution that leads to correct results will be duly marked

**a.** For: **[0.5p]**

$R \sim t^{\alpha} \cdot E^{\beta} \cdot \rho^{\gamma}$ **[0.1p]**

$L = T^{\alpha} \cdot \left(M \cdot L^{2} \cdot T^{-2}\right)^{\beta} \cdot \left(M \cdot L^{-3}\right)^{\gamma}$ **[0.1p]**

$$\begin{cases} \alpha - 2\beta = 0 \\ 2\beta - 3\gamma = 1 \\ \beta + \gamma = 0 \end{cases}$$

**[0.1p]**

$\alpha = \dfrac{2}{5} \qquad \beta = \dfrac{1}{5} \qquad \gamma = -\dfrac{1}{5}$ **[0.1p]**

$R \sim t^{\frac{2}{5}} \cdot \left(\dfrac{E}{\rho}\right)^{\frac{1}{5}}$ **[0.1p]**

**b.** For: **[1.5p]**

$C \cong 1 \qquad R = t^{\frac{2}{5}} \cdot \left(\dfrac{E}{\rho}\right)^{\frac{1}{5}}$ **[0.1p]**

$log\ R = \dfrac{2}{5} \cdot log\ t + \dfrac{1}{5} \cdot log\ \dfrac{E}{\rho}$ **[0.3p]**

$y = A \cdot x + B$, where $\begin{cases} y = log\ R \\ x = log\ t \\ A = \dfrac{2}{5} \\ B = \dfrac{1}{5} log\ \dfrac{E}{\rho} \end{cases}$ **[0.2p]**

*Table 1*

| $t\ (s)$ | $R\ (m)$ | $log\ t$ | $log\ R$ |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | 550 | 0.60 | 2.74 |
| 8 | 700 | 0.90 | 2.85 |
| 16 | 950 | 1.20 | 2.98 |
| 28 | 1250 | 1.45 | 3.10 |
| 46 | 1500 | 1.67 | 3.18 |

*Note: Graf plot of* $\log R = f\left(\log t\right)$ *is optional* **[0.5p]**

The line fitting for the datasets in Table 1 has the following values of the slope and interception.

$$\begin{cases} A = 0.42 \\ B = 2.48 \end{cases}$$

**[0.2p]**

estimation of the amount of energy released at the atomic bomb explosion for which the images in Figure 1

$E \approx 3 \cdot 10^{12}\ J$ **[0.2p]**

**TOTAL SCORE: Theoretical Problem No. 2 – Part A** **2.0p**
